text:
liam: quick heads-up — since ~02:00 UTC we're seeing a spike of Xid 13 and Xid 31 on a subset of A10 cards in us-west2. pattern looks correlated with high-batch-size prompt traffic from tenant-h. attaching a short log sample below and a prometheus query I ran.

liam: logs:```kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1f.0): 13, PID=8421 in ...``````kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1f.0): 31, reason: ECC error``````

liam: prometheus query I ran: `sum by (xid) (increase(nv_xid_errors_total[5m]))` — shows Xid13: 45, Xid31: 22 in the last 5m for nodes with label gpu_type="A10" and region="us-west2".

maya: thanks liam. is this concentrated to a few cards or spread across the rack?

liam: looks concentrated to a ~6-card set on rack-usw2-b-14. same PCI bus IDs repeatedly in the logs.

tony: quick checklist: 1) soft-drain pods on affected nodes 2) capture full dmesg and `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` 3) run memtest on suspect cards if possible 4) consider permanent replace if ECC counts climb after reboot.

anika: curious if mix of big-batch token lengths triggers KV cache churn — we've seen Xid13 associated with long decode loops before. can we correlate with batch-shape?

liam: yes — cross-ref with request logs shows 80% of affected requests had batch sizes >= 64 and seq_len >= 2048. tenant-h uses an adapter that packs many short prompts into larger batches.

maya: is there an immediate mitigation to prevent customer impact? can we route tenant-h to other pools or lower their max batch size?

tony: routing: we can add a temporary policy in the smart-router to divert tenant-h to h2-pool (non-A10) for a few hours. fallback: clamp max_batch_size=32 for tenant-h via runtime config. both low risk.

liam: doing a controlled soft-drain on the 6 suspect cards now (`kubectl annotate node ... soft-drain=true`) — will keep them in the pool for low-priority jobs only. posting status in 5m.

infra-bot: deploybot: node-uw2-b-14-03 annotated soft-drain=true by liam at 02:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

maya: collect the following for postmortem: PCI IDs, ECC counters pre/post reboot, nvlink errors, firmware versions, tenant batch-size histograms, and infra-scheduler events.

liam: collected dmesg + `nvidia-smi -q` snapshot and uploaded to /mnt/infralogs/3612349999/xid-sample.tar.gz. ECC counters show single-bit corrections increased from 120->187 after the spike window.

anika: could also be a kernel driver regression; any recent driver bumps in us-west2?

tony: checked infra changelog — no driver rollouts in last 48h for that rack. only scheduler tweak rolled out yesterday (no changes to GPU drivers).

maya: propose: 1) keep soft-drain for next 24h 2) re-run MEMTEST overnight (low-priority window) 3) if errors persist after reboot+memtest, schedule RMA for those cards and mark as suspect in inventory 4) apply routing rule for tenant-h to lower batch sizes + temporary pool shift.

liam: agree. I'll also add a per-tenant throttle check to the router so future bursts trigger a graceful backoff instead of big bulk packs.

anika: add an eval to run against tenant-h's outputs to see if lowering batch size regresses quality — want to avoid unexpected quality drops.

tony: logging note: we should start emitting xid_code as a structured tag in the GPU error exporter so the incident graphs can filter by xid. current labels are noisy. I'll file infra ticket.

liam: filed INFRA-4821: "emit nv_xid_code as label on gpu_error metric" — linking in postmortem.

maya: thanks all — mitigation steps in motion. ping me if errors rise again or if any node shows new Xid codes (48/79) — that would change the plan. :eyes:

liam: updating thread after memtest run (will post results later).

infra-bot: memtest-runner: scheduled memtest on node-uw2-b-14-03 for 23:00 UTC (low-prio window).

liam: final note — tenant-h ops pls: please limit packer size temporarily. I'll coordinate with your eng contact. @tenant-h-ops

maya: closing interim triage. we will open a full postmortem if RMAs are required. :hammer:
